  "reasoning": "The contract declares a purely combinational module (clocking.is_sequential is false, both outputs at latency_cycles 0), so the dispatch is `evaluate` and there is no state to carry between calls. REQ-0000 fixes sum = a XOR b (half-adder sum, explicitly with no carry-in) and REQ-0001 fixes cout = a AND b (carry-out asserted only when both input bits are 1); together they cover both declared output ports, so every output is written on every call. All four ports are one bit wide: XOR and AND of two 1-bit values cannot exceed one bit, but I mask both the inputs on read and the results on write so the model stays truthful to the declared port widths even if the harness ever presents a wider int for a or b -- an unmasked input would otherwise leak bit 1 and above into sum. The methods are pure functions of `i`: no imports, no randomness, no time, no I/O and no global or instance state. Nothing here is ambiguous -- the specification names the half adder outright and both requirements state the boolean function directly -- so `underdetermined` is empty.",

Inputs are masked to their declared\n    # 1-bit width before use, and the result is masked to the 1-bit\n    # width of the 'sum' output port.\n    a = self.mask(i['a'], 1)\n    b = self.mask(i['b'], 1)\n    o['sum'] = self.mask(a ^ b, 1)\n"
